subject: Hosted API rate discussion — blended commit, uplift for premium models and embeddings
messages:
From: Jordan Matthews <jmatthews@luminahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@luminahealth.com>, Lumina Health Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on ratecard uplift and blended commit for pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the rate card you sent last week. A couple of quick clarifications before we share internally:

- We plan to run a 3-month POC where ~60% of calls will use the standard chat model and ~40% will use a higher-capability "contextual" model (you previously labeled as premium). Your ratecard lists a 2.4x uplift for "premium" — is that applied to both prompt and completion tokens?

- We will also use embeddings for semantic search in one flow. The quote shows a separate embedding unit price but doesn't indicate how embeddings count against the committed token pool (if at all). Lumina prefers a single blended commit to simplify procurement; can premium model usage and embeddings be folded into a blended effective $/token for the commit?

- If we commit to 50M tokens/mo for 12 months, what is the overage rate, and is there a ramp discount for months 1–3? Our procurement team tends to want staged commitments.

Appreciate a short write-up or sample invoice line items we can show procurement.

Best,
Jordan

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@luminahealth.com>, Lumina Health Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-29T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on ratecard uplift and blended commit for pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. I pulled together a concise response and attached a sample rate card + SOW draft for procurement. Key points up front:

1) Premium uplift mechanics
- The premium multiplier (listed as 2.4x in the draft) applies to billable token units (both prompt + completion). We bill tokens consumed by the model variant serving the request.
- For transparency we can break line items into: standard-chat tokens, premium-chat tokens, and embedding units.

2) Blended commit approach (recommended for procurement simplicity)
- We can offer an effective blended $/token for the committed pool that treats embeddings as a separate unit but converts them to token-equivalents for the purposes of the commit. Example conversion we propose: 1 embedding unit = 0.6 token-equivalents for billing against the commit. (This keeps vector-heavy workloads from consuming the committed chat pool unfairly.)
- Using that conversion, we can produce a blended $/token that already includes expected mix and premium uplift. See sample calc below.

3) Ramp and overage
- Staged ramp: months 1–3 at 60% / 80% / 100% of the committed monthly token volume. During ramp months we apply the committed rate to the actual usage up to the ramped amount; any excess is billed at the overage rate.
- Overage rate: We typically set overage at 1.75x the committed blended $/token for that tier (negotiable for large commits).

4) Pilot-specific concession
- For a 3-month POC we can provide a temporary 12% pilot discount on the blended committed rate (applies only to committed buckets, not overage). The discount requires a short SOW and a commitment to the 12-month term after POC if you want the discounted long-term pricing.

Sample blended calc (illustrative):
- Commit: 50M tokens/mo
- Expected mix: 60% standard-chat, 30% premium-chat, 10% embeddings
- Base list: standard-chat $0.0009/token, premium multiplier 2.4x -> premium-list $0.00216/token, embedding unit $0.0045/unit -> converted at 0.6 token-eq = $0.0027/token-equivalent
- Weighted blended list $/token = (0.6*0.0009) + (0.3*0.00216) + (0.1*0.0027) = $0.00123/token
- Committed negotiated rate (example): apply 18% committed discount -> $0.001009/token -> with pilot 12% additional off committed -> $0.000888/token for months where pilot discount applies

I attached redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf and a draft SOW (Lumina_SOW-draft.docx). Aditya — I looped you in to confirm the grid and to propose the overage cadence for this tier.

Next steps: If this approach looks acceptable, I can send a DocuSign-ready quote and SOW for procurement.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-07-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on ratecard uplift and blended commit for pilot

Jordan / Soojin — quick pricing note from our side. Agreement looks straightforward; a couple of optional levers to make procurement happier without sacrificing economics:

- Alternative uplift model: instead of a flat 2.4x on premium tokens, offer a tiered uplift that drops at higher premium volume thresholds (e.g., 2.4x up to 10M premium tokens/mo, 2.1x 10–25M, 1.9x >25M). This rewards adoption of the premium model while protecting your unit economics at scale.

- Embedding bundling: offer a bundled embedding allowance (e.g., 5M embedding units/mo included in commit, with excess billed at a discounted embedding overage). This reduces the conversion complexity for procurement.

- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing with a quarterly true-up for blend mismatches. If actual mix diverges by >15% from the committed mix for two consecutive quarters, we propose a modest account review and a one-time adjustment to the effective blended rate to re-align economics.

If Lumina wants to keep procurement simple, we can ship a single-line summarized quote showing: committed tokens, effective blended $/token, pilot discount applied, and the DocuSign link. SOW will attach usage caps and ramp schedule.

Aditya Rao
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on ratecard uplift and blended commit for pilot

Thanks — that level of detail is exactly what procurement needs. A couple of small asks before we sign:

1) Can you formalize the premium volume thresholds (Aditya suggested) in the quote so procurement can see savings at scale?
2) We want the pilot discount to be unconditional on converting to 12 months; procurement typically balks at conditional discounts. Could you make the 12% pilot discount unconditional for the 3-month POC only?
3) SLA: we need a 99.9% availability SLA for hosted API or a credit schedule equivalent for the POC window.

If you can send a one-page summary quote with those three items and a DocuSign link, we can route to procurement today.

—Jordan
